name: Interview mental maths, set 3
description: Mental maths at interview speed: products, division, percent chains, odds, estimates, sequences, roots, work rates, net scores and rankings. Each item keeps its own schedule.

items.prose: Work it out in your head.
items.question: What is $73 \times 28$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Round 28 up to 30, then take off what you added.

byKey.one-73: You took off one 73. Rounding 28 up to 30 adds two 73s, so take off 146.

explain.text: $73 \times 30 = 2190$. You added two 73s, so take off 146. That leaves $2190 - 146 = 2044$.

items.question: What is $4357 \div 13$, to one decimal place?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the whole part first, then turn the remainder into a decimal.

byKey.cut-off: You cut the decimal off instead of rounding. The remainder 2/13 is 0.154, which rounds up to 0.2.
byKey.decimal-slip: You slipped a decimal place. 13 × 300 is already 3,900, so the answer is in the hundreds.

explain.text: $13 \times 335 = 4355$, leaving a remainder of 2. Then $2/13 \approx 0.154$, which rounds to 0.2. So the answer is 335.2.

items.prose: A share rises 20%, then falls 15%, then rises 10%.
items.question: What is its net change, as a percentage to one decimal place?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply the growth factors 1.2, 0.85 and 1.1.

byKey.added: You added the three moves. Each move acts on the new price, so multiply the factors.
byKey.two-moves: You stopped after two moves. The last +10% acts on 1.02, giving 1.122.

explain.text: $1.2 \times 0.85 = 1.02$. Then $1.02 \times 1.1 = 1.122$. So the net change is +12.2%.

items.prose: A bookmaker quotes odds of 3 to 7 on an outcome: a £7 stake wins £3 profit.
items.question: What chance does the price imply, as a percentage?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the chance at which the bet has zero expected profit.

byKey.flipped: You put the profit on top. The stake, 7, goes on top: 7/(3 + 7).
byKey.ratio: You divided 3 by 7. The bottom is the total of the two sides, 10.

explain.text: At chance p the bet is fair when $3p = 7(1 - p)$. So $10p = 7$ and $p = 0.7$. Odds of 3 to 7 imply a 70% chance.

options.why: You rounded every factor down. The errors add up to about 7% low.
You rounded every factor up, to 7 × 15 × 3.2 = 336. That is about 8% high.
You slipped a decimal place. 6.82 × 14.7 is about 100, and 100 × 3.1 is 310.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Pair the first two factors into a round number first.

explain.text: $6.82 \times 14.7$ is close to $7 \times 14.3 \approx 100$. Then $100 \times 3.1 = 310$. The exact product is 310.79, so 310 is well within 3%.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Read every other term.

byKey.doubled-last: You doubled the last term. Two sequences are woven together, and the next term belongs to the first: 2, 4, 8.
byKey.added-last: You added the last two terms. The odd places double on their own: 2, 4, 8, 16.

explain.text: The odd places run 2, 4, 8 and the even places 10, 20, 40. Each strand doubles. The seventh term is on the first strand: 16.

items.prose: Start from the guess 3.3, since $3.3^2 = 10.89$. One Newton step averages the guess with 11 divided by the guess.
items.question: What estimate of $\sqrt{11}$ does one step give, to two decimal places?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out 11/3.3, then average it with 3.3.

byKey.no-average: You stopped at 11/3.3 = 3.33. Average it with 3.3 to finish the step.
byKey.no-step: You kept the starting guess. One step moves it up, since $3.3^2$ is below 11.

explain.text: $11/3.3 = 3.3333$. The average of 3.3 and 3.3333 is 3.3167. That rounds to 3.32, and $\sqrt{11} = 3.3166$ to four places.

items.prose: A job takes 6 people 10 days. Everyone works at the same rate.
items.question: How many days does it take 4 people, and then 4 people working half-time?

options.why: You halved the time for half-time work. Half the hours means twice the days.
You scaled the days by 4/6. Fewer people take longer, so scale by 6/4.
You kept 10 days for 4 people. The job is 60 person-days, so 4 people need 15.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the job in person-days first.

explain.text: The job is 6 × 10 = 60 person-days. Four people need 60/4 = 15 days. Working half-time they do 2 person-days a day, so they need 30 days.

items.prose: A test has 80 questions. A right answer scores +1, a wrong one −1 and a skip 0. You get 63 right, 11 wrong and skip 6.
items.question: What is your net score?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the right answers and take off the wrong ones.

byKey.no-penalty: You left out the penalty. Each of the 11 wrong answers costs 1.
byKey.skips-cost: You charged the skips. A skip scores 0, so only the 11 wrong answers cost.

explain.text: Right answers give +63 and wrong ones −11. Skips score nothing. The net score is 63 − 11 = 52, and accuracy on the 74 answered is 85%.

items.prose: Five events. A: odds of 3 to 2 against. B: chance 5/12. C: chance 0.42. D: chance 7/17. E: odds of 4 to 3 against. Odds of 3 to 2 against mean 3 failures for every 2 successes.
items.question: Which lists them from least to most likely?

options.why: You listed them from most to least likely.
You read the odds as chances for. Odds of 3 to 2 against give 2/5, not 3/5.

feedback.correct: Correct. A, D, B, C, E.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Turn each into a decimal to three places.

explain.text: As decimals, A is 2/5 = 0.400, D is 7/17 ≈ 0.412 and B is 5/12 ≈ 0.417. Then C is 0.420 and E is 3/7 ≈ 0.429. So the order is A, D, B, C, E.
